chk.none: No problems found in the draft.

chk.server_stale_hint: You edited the draft after this check. Check again to see the server's view of the current draft.
chk.server_admin: Only an admin can run the server's validator.

diff.title: Changes against the current file

apply.rollback_ok: Rolled back to the selected revision.

conflict.discard: Discard my edits and load latest
conflict.rediffed: Reloaded the current file. Your edits are kept; review the diff and apply again.

act.note.skillevaluator.evaluate_live: Spends router tokens: an agent runs the skill's eval cases in a sandboxed container for minutes (up to about an hour). It runs in the background; one live run at a time.

se.tiers_hint: Evaluate runs Tier 1 (static checks, plus an LLM judge through the router unless you pick static) and optionally Tier 2 (embedding deduplication, which needs the embeddings model). Tier 3 (live agent runs: the Skill Lift, with the skill minus without it) is the separate Tier 3 action: it runs in a sandboxed runner container through the skillevaluator-local wrapper, takes minutes (up to about an hour), spends router tokens and runs in the background, one at a time. Reports are kept in the console state dir; open one with Evaluate → Show a stored report.
dd.hint: Data Designer is a CLI the console runs on demand: it generates synthetic datasets from a config script through the lab router. The console keeps the run reports and up to the first 2,000 records per run; the full datasets land in ~/Datasets.
dd.records_admin_only: The generated rows are admin-only: they are model-written content. Viewers see the run details and the artifact list.
dd.scripts_note: Validate and apply execute this script on this machine with your user's privileges (that is how Data Designer loads a config builder). Review it before you run either.

dd.runs_empty_hint: Run Preview records or Create a dataset; runs are kept in the console state dir (newest 100).

dd.records_empty: No records stored for this run.
dd.records_cap: The console keeps at most the first 2,000 records per run (records.jsonl). The parquet files in the run directory always hold the full dataset.
dd.files_empty: No files recorded for this run.
dd.files_hint: The console lists the files but does not serve them; open them on disk.

dyn.go_dark: Router aliases that go dark while Dynamo holds the card
dyn.lifecycle_hint: Each button runs preflight first and then asks you to confirm the exact effect. These buttons start and stop only Dynamo's containers, with the compose files the running stack was started from (a variant such as Super VL keeps its override file). Dynamo is opt-in: while an exclusive engine holds one of the worker's cards, Up is refused; use the start command shown in the Dynamo status instead.

dyn.effect_down: Stops the Dynamo frontend and worker.
dyn.effect_restart: Restarts the Dynamo frontend and worker.

dyn.stop_sharing: Also stop {name}, the opt-in engine on this card (required for Up while it runs)
dyn.stop_sharing_hint: Without this, Up is refused. Only that one container is stopped; no other engine is ever stopped from here.
params.title: Tunables

params.err_choice: Not one of the allowed choices

params.effect_live: Writes the compose override. The changed parameters take effect without a restart.
params.confirm_override: The repository compose file is not modified.

err.module: This page's code did not load. If the console was just updated, your browser may still hold older files: reload with Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac).
err.network: Cannot reach the console backend. Check that it is running on 127.0.0.1:8793 and that this page is served from it.
err.401: Authentication is required. Set a bearer token with the key button in the top bar.
err.403: Not allowed. Either your role is viewer, or the request was rejected as cross-origin. Open the console from its own address.
err.409: Conflict: the file changed since you loaded it, or the target is busy. Reload and review before retrying.
err.413: The request body is too large (limit 1 MiB; config files 256 KiB). Shorten it and retry.
err.415: The server refused the content type. Reload the page to get a matching client.
err.421: The Host header was rejected. Open the console at http://127.0.0.1:8793 or http://localhost:8793.
err.429: Too many requests or open streams. Wait a few seconds, close other console tabs, and retry.
err.502: The console could not reach the upstream system. Check its status on the Overview page.
err.503: The console or the upstream system is unavailable right now. Check the Overview page and retry shortly.
dyn.preflight_viewer: Preflight runs a check through the console and is admin-only. Ask an admin to run Up, Down or Restart.
settings.restart_required: A saved change only takes effect after the console backend restarts.
intro.openshell: The sandbox gateway that contains Data Designer runs. It starts on demand, so stopped means off, not down. Its gateway, policy and provider files are read-only here: a web console never loosens a sandbox's trust policy.
intro.dcgm: GPU telemetry from this host's exporter and from the DCGM hosts Prometheus scrapes (loopback only). The counters file is editable; its check is a proxy for the field lists in the exporter image.
intro.aiperf: Load profiles against a live engine through the router. A profile run spends router capacity and takes minutes, so it asks for confirmation; one run at a time.
intro.guardrails: A NeMo Guardrails server with no internet egress. Rails configs are editable; a candidate is loaded in a network-less container before it is applied, and the server is restarted and checked afterwards.
intro.evaluator: Offline benchmark suites against router aliases. Datasets are fetched once by a human beforehand; runs themselves use no egress. A run spends router tokens and takes minutes.
gen.metrics_unavailable: The system reports no metrics right now.
intro.modelopt: Offline compression of a pinned checkpoint: quantization, REAP expert pruning or Minitron. A job takes a GPU for hours and writes a new checkpoint, so it asks for confirmation; the job runs in the background and the console reads its result.
intro.gym: Reinforcement-learning environments and rollouts, run contained: each Gym command runs in a client container on an internal network whose only way out is a router broker. A smoke run rolls out a few scored tasks through the router, so it spends tokens on a shared engine and asks first; it runs in the background and the console keeps only the numbers.
intro.flare: NVIDIA's research-prototype inference server (Rust), on sm120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090) and sm121 GPUs (one DGX Spark, or several as one engine). It serves a package prepared once per GPU family and tensor-parallel size, on that family. Every action goes through the lab launcher, which defines the targets, refuses to start unless a target's GPUs are free and never stops another engine. An experiment lane, off by default; the version shown is the pinned upstream commit.

rh.empty_hint: A run appears here once the system has finished one. Nothing is shown for a run that left no record.

gpu.fleet.title: GPU fleet heatmap
gpu.fleet.lead: Every GPU of every DCGM host the lab's Prometheus scrapes, over time: one row per GPU, one column per time step, the colour is the chosen value. A hatched cell means no data (the host was down or the exporter did not answer); it is never drawn as a low value.
gpu.fleet.alt: Heatmap of {metric} for {rows} GPUs on {hosts} hosts, {window}. One row per GPU, one column per time step.
gpu.fleet.truncated: Only the first {max} GPUs are shown; the server stops there.
gpu.fleet.merged: The server answers one point per {step}; neighbouring points are averaged into columns of {bin} to fit the screen.
gpu.fleet.empty: No GPU history in this window
gpu.fleet.empty_hint: Prometheus has no DCGM samples for {window}. Check the hosts above, and the dcgm_prometheus_jobs setting.
gpu.fleet.unsupported: This console build has no fleet history
gpu.fleet.unsupported_hint: The server answered 404 for GET /systems/dcgm/fleet. Update the console backend; the Status tab still shows this host's GPUs.
gpu.busy.title: Is it really busy?
gpu.busy.lead: Utilisation is the share of time ANY kernel was running, so one small kernel can read 100%. The graphics, tensor and DRAM activity say how much of the chip actually worked. All figures are means over the window.
gpu.busy.none: No per-GPU utilisation in this window.
gpu.busy.say_busy: At least one engine is above 50% of its cycles.
gpu.busy.say_light: Kernels are running, but no engine is above 50%.
gpu.busy.say_misleading: Utilisation is high, yet no engine is above 25%: a kernel is running, not much work is done.
gpu.busy.say_util_only: The exporter does not report the profiling fields (graphics, tensor, DRAM), so only utilisation can be shown.
gpu.busy.say_unknown: No utilisation was reported in this window.
gpu.mem.title: Memory
gpu.mem.hint: Used, reserved and free memory of each GPU. Reserved is memory the driver or firmware holds back; it is not available to a model.
gpu.power.title: Power against its limit
gpu.power.lead: Draw of each GPU with the power limit it is held to. Close to the limit, the clock is throttled for power.
gpu.power.none: No power figures in this window.
gpu.power.no_limit: The exporter does not report a power limit for this GPU.
gpu.power.near: Highest draw {peak} is within 5% of the {limit} limit.
gpu.energy.title: Energy over the window
gpu.energy.lead: What each GPU used, from the exporter's energy counter (not from averaging power samples).
gpu.energy.none: No energy counter was reported in this window, or it has fewer than two samples.
gpu.energy.reset_note: The counter restarted at least once in this window, so the figure is a lower bound.
gpu.viol.title: Throttle violations
gpu.viol.lead: The share of time the clock was held back, by reason, from the exporter's violation counters. Only the reasons that throttled are drawn; every reason is in the table.
gpu.viol.quiet_say: No reason held the clock back in this window.
gpu.viol.say: The clock was held back for the reasons below.
gpu.viol.reset_note: A counter restarted in this window; the rate is not drawn across the restart.
gpu.remap.title: Remapped rows
gpu.remap.lead: Memory rows the GPU has retired and replaced. A growing uncorrectable count, or a remap failure, means the memory is wearing out.
gpu.remap.none: The exporter reports no remapped-row figures.
gpu.remap.unavailable: The exporter is not answering, so remapped rows cannot be read.
gpu.tl.title: XID errors and diagnostics
gpu.tl.hint: A lane per GPU: a diamond is an XID error, a circle a diagnostic run (✓ pass, ! warning, ✕ fail). Select a mark for its details.
gpu.tl.alt: Timeline of {count} XID errors and diagnostics on {lanes} GPUs, {window}.
gpu.tl.empty_hint: Nothing of either kind happened in {window}.
gpu.tl.outside: {count} older events are outside this window.
routing.filter_note: A route or model filter is on. The cards show only that name and shares are of the rows shown. The tier card is not filtered: the server counts tiers on their own.
sy.flow.title: Decision flow
sy.flow.lead: Where the stage routers sent requests: from the decision source (what decided) to the target that took it. Widths are the share of decisions over the window.
sy.flow.none_hint: Switchyard reported no decision counters. Pass-through routes make no decisions; the stage routers count them once a request has been routed.
sy.flow.two_col_note: The counters say which source decided and which target took the request, but not which route it came in on, so the routes are listed on their own below, not as a column.
sy.flow.route_not_applied: The route filter cannot narrow this flow: its counters carry no route. It still filters the route list.
sy.flow.filtered_out: The current filter leaves no decision to draw.
sy.flow.alt: Flow chart of {total} routing decisions over {window}, in {cols} columns.
sy.flow.last_records: The calls among the newest {count} routing records (not a time window)
sy.models.title: Models
sy.models.lead: What each model did over {window}: how long its calls took, how many failed, how much of the prompt came from cache, and the largest context it was given.
sy.models.none_hint: Switchyard has reported no per-model counters, or the filter leaves none.
sy.models.note: Latency is the mean of the window's p50 and p99 samples. The error rate is errors over calls in the window; it is an en dash when either counter is missing or no call was made.
sy.heat.title: Calls per model over time
sy.heat.lead: The call rate of each model, one row per model. A hatched cell has no data (a stats reset or a gap); an idle model is the lowest step.
sy.heat.none: No call counts in this window
sy.heat.none_hint: Switchyard reported no per-model call counter, or fewer than two samples.
sy.heat.alt: Heatmap of the call rate of {models} models over {window}, in calls {unit}.
sy.fb.title: Fallbacks and routing overhead
sy.fb.lead: Fallbacks are requests that could not go to the first choice (the context did not fit, the target was down). The routing overhead is the time Switchyard itself adds.
sy.fb.reset_note: A counter restarted in this window; the rate is not drawn across the restart.
sy.oh.title: Routing overhead
sy.out.title: What clients got
sy.out.lead: The outcome of each client request over {window}.
sy.out.none_hint: Switchyard reported no client response counter, or fewer than two samples.
dynv.latency_lead: For the window: the quantiles of the requests that finished since the previous poll. Since start: the quantiles over everything the frontend has served; they move slowly.
dynv.ttft_window: Time to first token, for the window
dynv.ttft_start: Time to first token, since start
dynv.phase_hint: Queue, prefill and decode, from the worker's own phase histograms. Quantiles of different phases do not add up exactly (the p95 of a sum is not the sum of the p95s), so read the stack as a guide to what dominates.
dynv.phase_partial: The worker reports only some phases for {q}, so its total is a lower bound.
dynv.load_hint: Requests running and waiting, KV cache usage and preemptions on one time axis, each on its own scale.
dynv.cap_none_hint: The worker reports none until it has loaded the model.
dynv.spec_hint: How often the draft token at each position was accepted by the target model, since the worker started.
dynv.ev_off: Dynamo is off (no frontend, worker or mocker container is running), so there are no logs to show. Start it from the Lifecycle tab.
dynv.ev_unknown: Dynamo's state could not be read ({why}), so its logs probably cannot be read either.
dynv.ev_empty_hint: New lines from the Dynamo containers appear here live. They are log text, shown as plain text; the server replaces secret-looking patterns, so treat them as sensitive.
dynv.ev_lead: The recent log lines of the Dynamo containers, newest first, live while this tab is open. Before a line leaves the server the console replaces secret-looking patterns in it; the redaction is pattern-based, so treat the lines as sensitive.
dynv.ev_redacted: Lines are shown as plain text and are cut at 400 characters by the server.
dynv.ev_none_match_hint: Turn a level back on, or clear the filters.
dynv.no_requests: No request finished in this window, so there are no latency figures (an idle worker is not a latency of 0).
dynv.cap_hint: As the worker reports them; where several models are loaded, the largest value across them.
rv.not_found: The console has no data of this kind for the run (an older console, or the run's files are gone). The charts above still work.
viz.req_error: Request {i}: failed with HTTP {code}, started at {start}
viz.db_row: {name}: without the skill {without}, with the skill {with}, change {delta}
apv.router_hop: These numbers include the router hop: AIPerf calls the LiteLLM router, not the engine, so they are what a client sees.
apv.select_hint: Select a run on the timeline above to see its percentile curves, HTTP phases and per-request view. Shift+click a second run to overlay it.
apv.scatter_hint: One marker per run: output tokens per second against the chosen latency. Colour and shape give the concurrency. Click a marker to select the run, Shift+click to compare it.
apv.scatter_alt: Throughput against {x}: {count} runs, one marker each.
apv.scatter_empty: None of the runs shown has both a throughput and this latency.
apv.scatter_skipped: {count} runs have no value for one of the two numbers and are left out; they are never drawn at zero.
apv.b_failed: Run B has no summary (it failed to load or did not record one): only run A is drawn.
apv.curves_hint: p1 to p99 of each latency for run A (solid line) and, when you pick a second run, run B (dashed line). The percentiles are spaced evenly so the slow tail stays readable.
apv.curves_none: Neither run recorded a latency percentile.
apv.curve_missing: Run {runs} did not record this metric: it has no line here.
apv.phases_title: Where a request spends its time (HTTP phases)
apv.phases_hint: Mean time per phase of one request, in the order they happen. Waiting is the server thinking.
apv.phases_none: This run did not record HTTP phase timings.
apv.phases_some_missing: One of the two runs recorded no HTTP phases: only the other is drawn.
apv.req_hint: Every request of the run as exported: the latency histogram, the requests laid out by worker over time, and the error codes.
apv.req_none: This run left no per-request export (it needs the records export level), so there is nothing to draw here.
apv.req_truncated: Showing {returned} of {total} requests, sampled evenly across the run.
apv.hist_note: {n} requests: median {p50}, p95 {p95}; {failed} failed and are on the error bars.
apv.swim_none: No request has a start and an end.
apv.swim_note: Drawing {shown} requests on {lanes} of {workers} workers (the busiest lanes; every failed request is kept).
apv.err_alt: {errors} of {total} requests failed, by HTTP code.
evv.none: No run with benchmark scores yet.
evv.default_run: No run is selected: showing the newest run, {run} ({time} UTC). Select one on the timeline above.
evv.ci_hint: The score of each benchmark for run A and, when you pick a second run, run B. The whisker is the confidence interval NeMo Evaluator reports; a run without one shows the bar only.
evv.no_ci_note: {count} results have no confidence interval (an older run): their bar has no whisker.
evv.ci_alt: Scores with confidence intervals for {count} benchmarks.
evv.matrix_hint: The newest score of each model on each benchmark, from the runs shown. A hatched cell has no run. Click a cell to select its run.
evv.matrix_alt: Newest score of {models} models on {benches} benchmarks.
evv.matrix_none: No run with a model and a score yet.
evv.cost_hint: One marker per benchmark result: how many tokens it used, or how long it took, against its score. Colour and shape give the benchmark. Click a marker to select the run.
evv.cost_none: No result has both a score and this cost figure.
evv.cost_skipped: {count} results have no figure for this cost (an older run) and are left out.
evv.fail_hint: The share of samples that failed, for the newest result of each model on each benchmark, highest first.
evv.fail_alt: Failure rate of {count} model and benchmark pairs.
evv.fail_none: No result recorded a failure rate.
evv.fail_missing: {count} pairs have no failure rate recorded and are left out.
gymv.default_run: No run is selected: showing the newest run with rewards, {run} ({time} UTC). Select one on the timeline above.
gymv.dist_hint: How many tasks of the run earned each reward, for run A and, when you pick a second run, run B beside it.
gymv.dist_alt: Reward distribution: {a} rewards for run A, {b} for run B.
gymv.stats: {n} rewards, mean {mean}, {full} at full reward, {zero} at zero
gymv.run_no_rewards: Run {run} recorded no per-task rewards (an older run, or one that did not finish): it has no bars.
gymv.rollouts_hint: Of the rollouts of each run, how many produced a reward and how many did not. The newest runs, oldest first.
gymv.trend_title: Mean reward and pass@1 by model
gymv.trend_hint: One line per model across the runs shown, oldest on the left. Click a point to select the run, Shift+click to compare it.
gymv.trend_alt: Trend of {metric} by model: {points} points from {runs} runs.
mov.running_hint: How long a running job has run, against what a finished job of the same method took (the median). A job that runs much longer than that stands out.
mov.typical_line: a finished job of this method takes about {typical}
mov.no_typical: no finished job to compare with
mov.typical_tip: A finished job of the same method takes {typical} (median)
mov.running_alt: Age of {count} running jobs against the typical duration.
mov.timeline_hint: Duration of each job, oldest first. The colour is the method; the outline, glyph and word are the verdict. Click a bar to select the job.
mov.size_hint: The size of the base model and of the compressed output per job, with the output as a share of the base. Only jobs that recorded both sizes.
mov.size_alt: Base and output size of {count} jobs.
mov.size_none: No job recorded both a base and an output size.
mov.size_missing: {count} finished jobs have no size pair (a failed or interrupted job) and are left out.
skv.default_run: No run is selected: showing the newest run that has this, {run} ({time} UTC). Select one on the timeline above.
skv.heat_hint: Status and worst finding severity of each validator for the latest {runs} Tier 1 runs shown, oldest on the left. Click a column to select the run.
skv.heat_alt: Validator status for {validators} validators over {runs} runs.
skv.heat_failed: {count} runs have no summary (it failed to load) and are left out.
skv.heat_none: The runs shown ran no validator.
skv.heat_no_runs: No Tier 1 run among the runs shown.
skv.letters: Letters: C critical, H high, M medium, L low, I info (the worst finding).
skv.key.warn: Passed with medium or low findings
skv.key.bad: Failed, or a critical or high finding
skv.key.muted: Did not run or did not finish
skv.rubric_hint: The score of each rubric criterion for run A (and run B), with a tick when it passes, and the quality dimensions. Criterion text is not shown (it is skill-written content); only its id.
skv.rubric_none: Select a run to see its rubric.
skv.rubric_empty: This run has no Tier 1 rubric.
skv.pass_key: A tick after the score: the criterion passes; a cross: it fails.
skv.b_unavailable: Run B has no summary (it failed to load or has none of this kind): only run A is drawn.
skv.lift_hint: For each agent and each metric: the score without the skill (a hollow circle) and with it (a filled diamond), and the lift between them.
skv.influence: A skill can influence its own Tier 3 score.
skv.influence_more: The agent that runs with the skill reads the skill's text, so a high lift is evidence, not proof; compare it with the Tier 1 findings.
skv.lift_none: Select a run to see its Tier 3 lift.
skv.lift_dir: A triangle up is a better score with the skill, a triangle down a worse one.
ddv.profile_hint: What each column of the run's records holds: the types, how many values are missing, how many differ, and the spread of lengths and numbers.
ddv.no_rows: This run wrote no records, so there is nothing to profile.
ddv.no_columns: The records of this run have no columns to profile.
ddv.types_hint: How many values of each column are text, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays or missing.
ddv.columns_hint: Missing share, distinct values, and the range of text lengths and of numbers.
ddv.range_key: Ranges read: minimum, median, 95th percentile, maximum. The bar runs from the minimum to the maximum; the filled mark is the median, the hollow one the 95th percentile. A greater-or-equal sign means the count was capped.
ddv.top_hint: The ten most frequent values of a column with few distinct values. These are model-written content, so only an admin sees them.
ddv.top_hidden: The most frequent values and the numeric ranges are shown to admins only: they are real values of the model-written rows. Types, missing share, distinct counts and text lengths are the same for everyone.
ddv.top_none: No column has few enough distinct values to list its most frequent ones.
ddv.top_cover: These values cover {pct} of the column's values.
ddv.timeline_hint: How long each run took, by script, and how many records it wrote against how many it was asked for. Oldest first. Click a bar to select the run.
ddv.records_alt: Records requested and written for {count} runs.
ddv.records_none: No run recorded how many records it wrote.
viz.req_error_nocode: Request {i}: failed without an HTTP code, started at {start}
ddv.truncated: The route read only part of the records (at most 2,000 rows) or dropped columns (over 200, or with an invalid name), so these figures describe the part it read.
strip.summary: {noun}: up {pct} of the time it was sampled in the {window}. {downs}
strip.none: No samples of this in the {window}, so there is nothing to draw.
grv.title: Rails and availability
grv.rails_hint: What a request passes through in each rails config the server serves: the input rails in order, the main model, then the output rails. Only the names of the flows are shown; the console never reads or shows prompt text or Colang content.
grv.rails_empty_hint: The server lists no config, or the console cannot read any config files.
grv.rails_unsupported: This console build has no rails route
grv.rails_unsupported_hint: The rail pipeline needs a console with the 9.16 backend. The rest of the page works without it.
grv.streaming_none: No streaming settings in this config
grv.up_hint: Whether the Guardrails server answered, from the console's own polls (the gr.up metric). A tall bar is a period it was down, a low bar a period it was up. The strip follows the window above.
grv.up_none: No samples of the server's state in the {window}.
grv.probes_hint: For each check run: what the rails answered to each of the three fixed probes, against what they should have answered. A benign prompt should be allowed; a jailbreak and a harmful prompt should be blocked. Click a column header to select that run above.
grv.matrix_alt: {runs} check runs by {probes} probes. {slips} runs had an answer that was not as expected, {errors} runs had a probe error.
grv.matrix_none: No check run with probe results to draw.
grv.not_reached: not run (the check stops at the first probe that fails)
grv.latency_hint: The time each probe took, in ms; darker is slower, on one scale for every cell. A probe that timed out is flagged.
grv.latency_alt: Latency of each probe over {runs} check runs; the slowest was {max}.
grv.latency_none: No latency was recorded for these runs.
grv.hidden: {count} older runs are not drawn (the newest {shown} fit this width); the run history above has them all.
grv.facts_slips_one: 1 run with an answer not as expected
grv.facts_slips_other: {count} runs with an answer not as expected
osv.title: Sandboxes over time
osv.title_hint: Read-only: nothing here changes a sandbox or a policy.
osv.lifecycle_hint: One lane per sandbox, from the gateway's lifecycle events (created, phase changes, deleted). A bar ends in an arrow while the sandbox still exists and in a cross where it was deleted. Click a lane to read its policy decisions below.
osv.lifecycle_empty: No sandbox activity in this window
osv.lifecycle_empty_hint: No sandbox was created, changed or deleted in the {window}. Pick a longer window.
osv.lane_pick: Press to read its policy decisions
osv.lane_pick_gone: Deleted: there is no log to read
osv.lanes_hidden: {count} more sandboxes are not drawn (the {shown} newest are).
osv.events_partial: The console reads the newest 500 lifecycle events, so the oldest sandboxes of a long window may be missing.
osv.pick_gone: Sandbox {name} was deleted: its log is gone, so there are no decisions to read.
osv.phases_hint: How many sandboxes were in each phase over the window (the gateway's own list, polled by the console). A step holds between samples; a gap is a period in which nothing was sampled.
osv.phases_none_window: No sandbox existed in this window.
osv.dec_hint: The allow and deny decisions in one sandbox's log (the supervisor's OCSF lines), by category over time. A denied decision is the policy doing its job: it is drawn hatched with a cross. Only the category, kind and target are shown, never a command or file content.
osv.dec_no_sandbox_hint: A decision log can only be read for a sandbox that is in the gateway's list. Data Designer creates one per run and deletes it afterwards.
osv.dec_gone: Nothing to read for this sandbox
osv.dec_gone_hint: The console answered "unknown sandbox": it may have been deleted since the list was read, or this console build has no decisions route. Refresh to read the list again.
osv.dec_failed: The decisions could not be read
osv.dec_empty: No policy decision in this log
osv.dec_empty_hint: The log of {name} holds no allow or deny decision yet.
osv.dec_truncated: The log has more than the {max} newest decisions the console reads; older ones are not shown.
osv.dec_skipped: {count} log lines were not decisions the console could classify and are left out.
osv.dec_alt: Policy decisions of {name}: {total} in {lanes} categories, {allowed} allowed and {denied} denied
osv.dec_none_denied: No decision in this log was denied.
flv.title: Where Flare can run
flv.grid_hint: Every target the launcher knows: where it runs, on which chip, in what state and how many packages are prepared for it. A target whose GPU another engine holds is busy, not broken: Flare never stops another engine.
flv.grid_none: The launcher reports no target (is flare-local on the console's PATH?).
flv.engine_hint: From the engine's own counters; they exist only while a target serves.
flv.none_serving: No target is serving, so there are no engine counters to draw. They appear when a target starts.
flv.rates_hint: Rates of the engine's counters, one line per target. A counter that restarts leaves a gap, never a spike.
flv.mix_hint: Three counters the engine keeps separately, stacked so they can be compared. The console draws what the engine reports and does not add or subtract them for you.
flv.resets_note_one: {target}: the engine restarted once in this window; the totals count what it accumulated since the restart, so they are a lower bound.
flv.resets_note_other: {target}: the engine restarted {count} times in this window; the totals count what it accumulated since each restart, so they are a lower bound.
flv.load_hint: Requests the engine is working on (active) and requests waiting for a slot (pending), per target.
flv.load_over_time: Over time (the highest in each bucket)
ovw.problems_hint: Counts only: the problems themselves, with their fix commands, are on the system cards below.
ovw.strip_alt: Up and down over the last hour. {summary}
ovw.strip_none: No up or down samples in the {window}.
audv.title: Activity
audv.stat_denied_sub: requests refused before a handler are not audited, so they are not counted here
audv.days_hint: Audited calls that change something, per UTC day, stacked by system. The busiest systems are named; the rest are summed as other. A day with no audited action is a real zero.
audv.days_empty: No audited actions in this window
audv.days_empty_hint: Nothing was changed through the console in the {window}.
audv.matrix_title: Who changed what: actor by system
audv.matrix_hint: Each cell is the number of audited actions one actor (the key's alias) made on one system in the window; darker is more. Click a cell to open the log for that actor and system.
audv.matrix_empty: No actor activity in this window
audv.matrix_alt: Actions by {actors} actors on {systems} systems, {total} in all
audv.actors_hidden: {count} quieter actors are not drawn (the {shown} busiest are).
audv.errors_hint: Audited calls that ended with an error status (HTTP 400 and above), counted per time bucket. A bucket with none is a real zero.
audv.errors_none: No audited call ended in an error in the {window}.
audv.dropped: {count} rows of the summary were not understood and are left out.
audv.unsupported: This console build has no audit summary
audv.unsupported_hint: The summary needs a console with the 9.16 backend. The Log tab works without it.
audv.count_capped: Showing the newest {count} calls; narrow the filters to see older ones.
audv.empty_filtered: No audited call matches these filters.
osv.dec_problem: The console could not read this sandbox's log: {message}
osv.dec_failed_hint: The gateway's log call failed; the console tries again on the next refresh.
osv.dec_sparse: This log holds only {count} decisions so far, so they are listed instead of drawn. A sandbox's log often holds little more than its SSH open.
grv.problem_configs_capped: More configs exist than the console lists; the rest are left out.
grv.problem_config_unreadable: Config {config} could not be read; it is listed with no rails.
grv.problem_config_too_large: Config {config} is too large to read; it is listed with no rails.
grv.problem_config_not_utf8: Config {config} is not valid UTF-8 text; it is listed with no rails.
grv.problem_config_yaml_error: Config {config} has a YAML error; it is listed with no rails.
grv.problem_config_not_a_mapping: Config {config} is not a YAML mapping; it is listed with no rails.
grv.problem_flows_dropped: {count} flow names in {config} were left out because they are not plain names.
grv.problem_flows_capped: {count} flows in {config} are not shown (there are too many).
grv.problem_main_model_dropped: The main model of {config} was left out because it is not a plain name.
audv.truncated: The summary lists the busiest actor and system pairs only (the answer was cut at its cap), so the smallest cells are missing.
strip.dips_one: No stretch was down for all of it; 1 stretch had a dip.
strip.dips_other: No stretch was down for all of it; {count} stretches had a dip.
